Document specific features of toxicity

Further investigations: FBC, UE, LFT, Paracetamol/Salicylate level, urine tox

alcohol ingestion 
TOXIC ALCOHOL INGESTION 
 
 
COMMON TOXIC ALCOHOLS 
METHANOL 
• 
Antifreeze, windshield wiper fluid, paint removers 
• 
Metabolised to formaldehyde > formic acid - HAGMA 
• 
Ocular effects: blurry vision, reduced visual acuity, photophobia, “snowstorm” 
vision 
• 
Neurological effects: Parkinsonism, transverse myelitis, basal ganglia 
haemorrhages, inebriation 
ETHYLENE GLYCOL 
 
 
 
 
 
 
SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT 
* DECONTAMINATION: Not recommended 
* ENHANCED ELIMINATION: Haemodialysis effective, usually required 
* pH CORRECTION: Sodabic boluses 1ml/kg 8.5% until pH > 7.2 
* SEIZURES: IV benzodiazepines. Monitor for arrhythmias/hypoglycaemia as cause 
* INTUBATION: Airway protection prior to ETOH administration 
* ANTIDOTE: Required for ethylene glycol/methanol ingestion 
• 
Fomepizole 15mg/kg loading, then 10mg/kg 12 hrly 
• 
Alcohol: 40% ethanol e.g. Vodka, 1.5 – 2 ml/kg loading dose, 
then 0.3ml/kg/hr maintenance via NGT. Continue until vital 
signs and lab values normalize or pt receives dialysis 
*COFACTORS: promote conversion to non-toxic metabolites 
• 
Ethylene glycol: pyridoxine 100mg QID, thiamine 100mg QID 
• 
Methanol: folic acid 50mg 4-6hrly 
*ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL: supportive Rx, PPI 
• 
Radiator antifreeze, brake fluid, metal cleaners 
• 
Metabolized to glycoaldehyde > glycolic acid > glycoxylic acid > oxalic acid. 
Artefactual lactic acidosis, HAGMA 
• 
Neurologic effects: coma, seizures, meningism, muscle spasms, ocular paralysis 
• 
Cardiopulmonary: tachycardia, hyperventilation, ARDS, heart failure 
• 
Hypocalcaemia, prolonged QT interval, acute renal failure due to calcium 
oxalate crystalluria
